summary: Defines the formal URN namespace identifier for EIDR identifiers, which uniquely identify motion picture and television content. It was replaced by RFC 7972.

eli5.summary: Every movie and show gets a unique code. This sets up the official naming for those codes. A later document replaced it.

questions: how do i identify a movie with eidr
subtitle: A standard naming scheme for unique identifiers of movies and TV shows.

tldr.problem: The entertainment industry needed a globally unique way to identify motion pictures and television content across different systems and databases.
tldr.mechanism: EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry) assigns unique digital object identifiers to audiovisual works and creates a formal URN namespace so these identifiers can be referenced as Uniform Resource Names.
tldr.outcome: Entertainment metadata systems can now use EIDR URNs (such as urn:eidr:10.5240:7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5) to uniquely identify content, replacing RFC 7302 with RFC 7972.

today: RFC 7302 was obsoleted by RFC 7972, an updated namespace definition. EIDR continues to assign unique identifiers to audiovisual content worldwide.

sections.title: Introduction to EIDR
sections.content:
EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry) identifiers are globally unique codes for motion pictures and television content. They are used to uniquely identify audiovisual works and their variants, such as different cuts of a film or regional versions of a show. The RFC defines the formal URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace for EIDR identifiers so they can be referenced consistently across systems.

EIDR identifiers are actually a special kind of DOI name (Digital Object Identifier), a system that provides persistent, globally unique identification for digital objects. The EIDR Association holds a unique DOI prefix ("10.5240") from the International Organization for Standardization.
sections.eli5: Movies and shows need codes so computer systems know which version they are talking about. This document sets up the official naming system for those codes.

sections.title: The EIDR Identifier and URN Format
sections.content:
An EIDR identifier consists of two parts: a DOI prefix (currently "10.5240") and a suffix defined by EIDR Association. The canonical representation is 10.5240/7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5. When used as a URN, this becomes urn:eidr:10.5240:7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5, replacing the forward slash with a colon because slash is a reserved character in URN syntax.

The suffix must follow the RP2079-SUFFIX syntax specified in the SMPTE standard, which consists of five groups of four hexadecimal digits separated by hyphens, followed by a check digit using the Mod 37,36 algorithm. This check digit ensures the identifier was typed or transmitted correctly.
sections.eli5: The code has two parts: a prefix that identifies EIDR (10.5240) and a unique suffix (like 7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5). The last character is a check digit to catch typos.

sections.title: Registration and Resolution
sections.content:
The EIDR Association registers each EIDR identifier with the ISO 26324 Registration Authority. Entities involved in motion picture and television production, distribution, and related services can become EIDR registrants by paying an annual membership fee. When registered, an EIDR identifier is associated with a unique URN and a set of metadata describing the audiovisual work.

EIDR identifiers can be resolved through the ISO 26324 Registration Authority's web service by making an HTTP GET request to http://doi.org/10.5240/7791-8534-2C23-9030-8610-5. If the identifier exists, the service returns an XML document containing the metadata; otherwise, it returns HTTP 404 Not Found. The EIDR Association also operates additional services with features such as confidential lookup using TLS and the ability to register new identifiers.
sections.eli5: Movie producers register their content with EIDR and get a unique code. Anyone can look up the code to find information about the movie.

sections.title: Use in the Entertainment Industry
sections.content:
EIDR identifiers are designed for use by producers, distributors, metadata aggregators, and audiovisual archives. The primary benefits are managing long or complex distribution chains (where a film has many versions for different regions and formats) and aggregating metadata from multiple sources. By using EIDR URNs, systems can reference the exact same work unambiguously, ensuring that metadata from different databases refers to the same content.

EIDR membership is open to bona fide members of the entertainment ecosystem, and the EIDR identifiers themselves can be used by anyone to identify and retrieve underlying metadata about a work, not just registrants.
sections.eli5: Movie studios, streaming services, and databases use EIDR codes to make sure everyone is talking about the same movie, especially when it has been changed for different countries or platforms.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 7302 defined the initial EIDR URN namespace and was replaced by RFC 7972, which provides an updated namespace definition. The EIDR system continues to be used for audiovisual content identification. The RFC ensures that EIDR identifiers follow the URN standard, making them compatible with tools and systems that process URNs.
sections.eli5: This document was replaced by RFC 7972, which provides an updated definition while the EIDR system itself continues to work the same way.
